'''Sir Konstantin Sergeevich Novoselov''' ({{lang-rus|Константи́н Серге́евич Новосёлов|
p=kənstɐnʲˈtʲin sʲɪrˈɡʲe(j)ɪvʲɪtɕ nəvɐˈsʲɵləf}}; born {{Nowrap|23 August}} 1974)<ref name="whoswho"/> is a Russian–British physicist. His work on [[graphene]] with [[Andre Geim]] earned them the [[Nobel Prize in Physics]] in 2010.<ref name="frs" /><ref name="scopus">{{Scopus|id=22135804300}}</ref><ref name="Nobel Announcement">{{cite web |date=5 October 2010 |title=Announcement of the 2010 Nobel Prize in Physics |url=https://www.nobelprize.org/nobel_prizes/physics/laureates/2010/press.html |access-date=2010-10-05 |publisher=[[The Nobel Foundation]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=The Royal Society, Dr. Kostya Novoselov |url=https://secure.royalsociety.org/ResearchFellows/holders/rp140026/konstantin-novoselov |access-date=5 October 2014 |archive-date=6 October 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141006115226/https://secure.royalsociety.org/ResearchFellows/holders/rp140026/konstantin-novoselov |url-status=dead }}</ref> Novoselov is a professor at the [[Centre for Advanced 2D Materials]], [[National University of Singapore]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite web | url=https://news.nus.edu.sg/press-releases/konstantin-novoselov-joins-nus |title = Nobel Laureate Konstantin Novoselov joins NUS}}</ref> and is also the [[Langworthy Professor]] of the [[School of Physics and Astronomy, University of Manchester|School of Physics and Astronomy]] at the [[University of Manchester]], and serves as President of [[Constructor University]] in Bremen, Germany.<ref>{{cite web |title=Ein Nobelpreisträger führt jetzt die Bremer Constructor University an |url=https://www.weser-kurier.de/bremen/ein-nobelpreistraeger-fuehrt-jetzt-die-bremer-constructor-university-an-doc84prhlkv2ptsxn58516 |publisher=Weser-Kurier |date=25 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Historische Premiere für Bremen: Nobelpreisträger Sir Konstantin Novoselov wird Präsident der Constructor University |url=https://nachrichten.idw-online.de/2026/02/24/historische-premiere-fuer-bremen-nobelpreistraeger-sir-konstantin-novoselov-wird-praesident-der-constructor-university?groupcolor=6 |publisher=IDW Nachrichten |date=24 February 2026}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last=Rohdenburg |first=Dierk |title=Constructor University beruft Physik‑Nobelpreisträger Konstantin Novoselov |work=Kreiszeitung |date=25 February 2026 |url=https://www.kreiszeitung.de/lokales/bremen/constructor-university-beruft-physik-nobelpreistraeger-konstantin-novoselov-94186118.html }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Historic first: Bremen Nobel Laureate Sir Konstantin Novoselov to lead Constructor University |publisher=Constructor University |date=24 February 2026 |url=https://constructor.university/news/historic-first-bremen-nobel-laureate-sir-konstantin-novoselov-lead-constructor-university }}</ref>

==Education ==
Konstantin Novoselov was born in [[Nizhny Tagil]], [[Soviet Union]], in 1974.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Overbye |first1=Dennis |author1-link=Dennis Overbye |title=Physics Nobel Honors Work on Ultra-Thin Carbon |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/10/06/science/06nobel.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=March 30, 2023 |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=October 5, 2010 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140924123720/http://www.nytimes.com/2010/10/06/science/06nobel.html?pagewanted=all |archive-date=2014-09-24}}{{cbignore}}</ref> He graduated from the [[Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology]] with a [[Master of Science|MSc]] degree in 1997,<ref name="whoswho"/> and was awarded a PhD from the [[Radboud University of Nijmegen]] in 2004<ref name="novoselovphd">{{cite thesis |degree=PhD |first=Konstantin S.|last=Novoselov |title=Development and applications of mesoscopic hall microprobes |publisher=Radboud University Nijmegen |year=2004 |url=http://repository.ubn.ru.nl/handle/2066/19519|author-link=Konstantin Novoselov}} {{ISBN|9090183663}}</ref> for work supervised by [[Andre Geim]].

Novoselov uses the nickname "Kostya" ([[diminutive]] of the name [[Konstantin]]).<ref>{{Cite web | url=https://www.kostyanovoselov.com/biography |title = Kostya Novoselov &#124; Biography}}</ref>

== Career ==
[[File:Konstantin Novoselov in lab.jpg|thumb|right|Konstantin Novoselov in his lab]]
Novoselov has published 475<ref>[http://www.researcherid.com/rid/G-9581-2014  Kostya Novoselov  G-9581-2014 ResearcherID]</ref> [[Peer review|peer-reviewed]] research papers on several topics including mesoscopic [[superconductivity]] ([[Hall effect|Hall magnetometry]]) as of January 2024 <ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Geim | first1 = A. K. | last2 = Dubonos | first2 = S. V. | last3 = Grigorieva | first3 = I. V. | last4 = Novoselov | first4 = K. S. | last5 = Peeters | first5 = F. M. | last6 = Schweigert | first6 = V. {{Cite journal | last1 = Novoselov | first1 = K. S. | last2 = Geim | first2 = A. K. | last3 = Dubonos | first3 = S. V. | last4 = Hill | first4 = E. W. | last5 = Grigorieva | first5 = I. {{Cite journal | last1 = Geim | first1 = A. K. | author-link = Andre Geim| last2 = Dubonos | first2 = S. V. | last3 = Grigorieva | first3 = I. V. | last4 = Novoselov | first4 = K. Y. | doi = 10.1038/nmat917 | title = Microfabricated adhesive mimicking gecko foot-hair | journal = Nature Materials | url = http://www.condmat.physics.manchester.ac.uk/pdf/mesoscopic/publications/geckotape/Naturemat_2003.pdf| volume = 2 | issue = 7 | pages = 461–463 | year = 2003 | pmid =  12776092|bibcode = 2003NatMa...2..461G | s2cid = 19995111 }}</ref> and [[graphene]].<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.graphene.manchester.ac.uk/explore/the-story-of-graphene/from-nanomaterial-to-global-explosion/ |title=From Nanomatierial to Global Expansion |author=<!--Staff writer(s); no by-line.--> |date=10 September 2014 |website=graphene.manchester.ac.uk/explore/the-story-of-graphene/from-nanomaterial-to-global-explosion/ |publisher=The University of Manchester |access-date=2014-10-09}}</ref><ref>

Kostya Novoselov participated in the [[Graphene Flagship]] project<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.graphene-flagship.eu|title=Graphene Flagship - Graphene Flagship|website=www.graphene-flagship.eu|access-date=31 October 2017}}</ref> – a €1&nbsp;billion initiative of the European Commission – and was featured in the official promotion movie of the project.<ref>{{cite news|title=Introducing graphene|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dTSnnlITsVg |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211221/dTSnnlITsVg |archive-date=2021-12-21 |url-status=live}}{{cbignore}}</ref>

Novoselov was the first Director of the [[National Graphene Institute]]<ref name="bigbet">{{Cite journal | last1 = Brumfiel | first1 = G.| title = Britain's big bet on graphene: Manchester institute will focus on commercial applications of atom-thick carbon sheets| doi = 10.1038/488140a | journal = Nature | volume = 488 | issue = 7410 | pages = 140–141 | year = 2012 | pmid =  22874942|bibcode = 2012Natur.488..140B | doi-access = free }}</ref><ref>[http://adsabs.harvard.edu/cgi-bin/nph-abs_connect?db_key=AST&db_key=PHY&db_key=PRE&qform=PHY&arxiv_sel=astro-ph&arxiv_sel=cond-mat&arxiv_sel=cs&arxiv_sel=gr-qc&arxiv_sel=hep-ex&arxiv_sel=hep-lat&arxiv_sel=hep-ph&arxiv_sel=hep-th&arxiv_sel=math&arxiv_sel=math-ph&arxiv_sel=nlin&arxiv_sel=nucl-ex&arxiv_sel=nucl-th&arxiv_sel=physics&arxiv_sel=quant-ph&arxiv_sel=q-bio&aut_logic=OR&author=Novoselov%2C+K.&ned_query=YES&sim_query=YES&start_mon=&start_year=&end_mon=&end_year=&ttl_logic=OR&title=&txt_logic=OR&text=&nr_to_return=200&start_nr=1&jou_pick=ALL&ref_stems=&data_and=ALL&group_and=ALL&start_entry_day=&start_entry_mon=&start_entry_year=&end_entry_day=&end_entry_mon=&end_entry_year=&min_score=&sort=SCORE&data_type=SHORT&aut_syn=YES&ttl_syn=YES&txt_syn=YES&aut_wt=1.0&ttl_wt=0.3&txt_wt=3.0&aut_wgt=YES&obj_wgt=YES&ttl_wgt=YES&txt_wgt=YES&ttl_sco=YES&txt_sco=YES&version=1 Astrophysics Data System]</ref><ref>{{Cite journal | last1 = Novoselov | first1 = K. Novoselov was also a recipient of a starting grant from the [[European Research Council]].<ref>
{{cite web
 |date=5 October 2010
 |title=Nobel Prize in Physics goes to ERC grantee Prof. Konstantin Novoselov
 |url=http://erc.europa.eu/pdf/Press_Release_Nobel_Prize_2010_ERC_Grantee.pdf
 |publisher=[[European Research Council]]
 |access-date=2010-10-10
}}</ref>

Kostya Novoselov made it into a shortlist of scientists with multiple hot papers for the years 2007–2008 (shared second place with 13 hot papers)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/ana/fea/09maraprFea/|title=The Hottest Research of 2007-08 - ScienceWatch.com|first=Clarivate|last=Analytics|website=archive.sciencewatch.com|access-date=31 October 2017}}</ref> and 2009 (5th place with 12 hot papers).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://archive.sciencewatch.com/ana/fea/10maraprFea/|title=2010 Mar/Apr - The Hottest Research of 2009 - ScienceWatch.com|first=Clarivate|last=Analytics|website=archive.sciencewatch.com|access-date=31 October 2017}}</ref>

In 2014 Kostya Novoselov was included in the list of the most highly cited researchers. He was also named among the 17 hottest researchers worldwide—"individuals who have published the greatest number of hot papers during 2012–2013".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://sciencewatch.com/sites/sw/files/sw-article/media/worlds-most-influential-scientific-minds-2014.pdf|title=ScienceWatch.com - Clarivate Analytics|first=Clarivate|last=Analytics|website=sciencewatch.com|access-date=31 October 2017}}</ref>

Novoselov joined the National University of Singapore's Centre for Advanced 2D Materials in 2019, making him the first Nobel laureate to join a Singaporean university.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/nobel-laureate-for-physics-to-join-nus|title=Nobel laureate for physics Konstantin Novoselov to join NUS|last=Ai-Lien|first=Chang|date=6 April 2019|work=The Straits Times|access-date=5 July 2019}}</ref> In 2021, he pioneered with [[Antonio H. Castro Neto]] a new research centre at the [[National University of Singapore]] called IFIM.<ref>{{Cite news |title=New NUS research centre to study functional intelligent materials with uses such as in artificial organs |newspaper=The Straits Times |date=7 October 2021 |url=https://www.straitstimes.com/singapore/new-nus-research-centre-to-study-functional-intelligent-materials-with-uses-such-as-in |last1=Shafeeq |first1=Syarafana }}</ref> With $200 million in funding over 10 years provided by the [[Ministry of Education (Singapore)|Ministry of Education]] and NUS, the centre will work on making ground-breaking discoveries into what are called functional intelligent materials.

== Awards and honours ==
[[Image:Nobel Prize 2010-Press Conference KVA-DSC 8019.jpg|250px|thumb|[[Peter Diamond]], [[Dale T. Mortensen]], [[Christopher A. Pissarides]], Konstantin Novoselov, [[Andre Geim]], [[Akira Suzuki (chemist)|Akira Suzuki]], [[Ei-ichi Negishi]], and [[Richard Heck]], Nobel Prize Laureates 2010, at a press conference at the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]] in Stockholm.]]
* 2007 Nicholas Kurti European Science Prize "to promote and recognise the novel work of young scientists working in the fields of Low Temperatures and/or High Magnetic Fields."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.oxford-instruments.com/businesses/nanotechnology/omicron-nanoscience/nicholas-kurti-european-science-prize|title=Leading provider of high technology tools and systems for research and industry - Oxford Instruments|website=Oxford Instruments}}</ref>
* 2008 Technology Review-35 Young Innovator<ref>{{cite magazine |url=http://www.technologyreview.com/tr35/Profile.aspx?Cand=T&TRID=732 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080910054322/http://www.technologyreview.com/tr35/Profile.aspx?Cand=T&TRID=732 |archive-date=2008-09-10 |url-status=dead |title=TR35 2008 Young Innovator: Kostya Novoselov, 34 |magazine=[[MIT Technology Review]] |access-date=30 March 2023}}{{cbignore}}</ref>
* 2008 University of Manchester Researcher of the Year.<ref name="ae-info.org">{{cite web|url=https://www.ae-info.org/ae/Member/Novoselov_Konstantin|title=Academia Europea Member Profile: Konstantin Novoselov|access-date=29 April 2024}}</ref>
* 2008 [[European Physical Society#Prizes|Europhysics Prize]], jointly with [[Andre Geim|Geim]], "for discovering and isolating a single free-standing atomic layer of carbon ([[graphene]]) and elucidating its remarkable electronic properties."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://c.ymcdn.com/sites/www.eps.org/resource/collection/E5F070A4-808E-4FD3-9217-06F321ED3CE1/EPS_CMD_prizeRecipients.pdf|title=EPS CMD Europhysics Prize Recipients|access-date=31 October 2017}}</ref><sup>,</sup><ref>
{{cite news
 |date=2 September 2008

 |title=Graphene pioneers bag Europhysics prize
 |publisher=Physics World
}}</ref>
* 2008 [[International Union of Pure and Applied Physics]] Young Scientist Prize, "for his contribution in the discovery of [[graphene]] and for pioneering studies of its extraordinary properties."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iupap.org/archiveyoungscientist.html|title=The IUPAP Young Scientist Prize|access-date=26 October 2011|archive-date=14 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120414231712/http://www.iupap.org/archiveyoungscientist.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>
* 2010 [[Nobel Prize in Physics]], jointly with [[Andre Geim]], "for groundbreaking experiments regarding the material graphene."<ref name="Nobel Announcement"/> Novoselov was the youngest Nobel laureate in physics since [[Brian David Josephson|Brian Josephson]] in 1973, and in any field since [[Rigoberta Menchú]] ([[Nobel Peace Prize|Peace]]) in 1992.{{citation needed|date=April 2024}}

==National Graphene Institute==
Novoselov led the academic team which overviewed the design, construction and launching of the [[National Graphene Institute]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.jesticowhiles.com/projects/education/national-graphene-institute/ |title=National Graphene Institute · Jestico + Whiles |access-date=10 October 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160405072522/http://jesticowhiles.com/projects/education/national-graphene-institute/ |archive-date=5 April 2016 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> He contributed with a number of unique architectural and technical solutions.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/multimedia/2015/oct/27/national-graphene-institute-a-video-tour/cws/article/multimedia/2015/oct/27/national-graphene-institute-a-video-tour|title=National Graphene Institute – a video tour – Physics World|date=27 October 2015}}</ref> The veil of the National Graphene Institute depicts formulae from his and Prof. A. Geim early works on graphene.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.lakesmere.com/Case-Study/161/National-Graphene-Institute/1.aspx#!prettyPhotogallery1/4/ |title=National Graphene Institute |access-date=10 October 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161011055312/http://www.lakesmere.com/Case-Study/161/National-Graphene-Institute/1.aspx#!prettyPhotogallery1/4/ |archive-date=11 October 2016 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> Also, Novoselov confirms that among the formulae several scientific jokes are hidden, though he has never revealed them.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.vice.com/en/article/inside-graphene-city-birthplace-of-a-wonder-material/|title=Inside Graphene City, Birthplace of a Wonder Material|date=2015-03-09|work=Motherboard|access-date=2018-05-20|language=en-us}}</ref>

He co-authored a book on the architecture of the National Graphene Institute.<ref>{{cite book | last1=Novoselov | first1=Kostya S | last2=Yaneva | first2=Albena | title=The New Architecture of Science: Learning from Graphene | publisher=WORLD SCIENTIFIC | date=2020 | isbn=978-981-12-2067-8 | doi=10.1142/11840 | url=https://www.worldscientific.com/worldscibooks/10.1142/11840 | access-date=2026-08-26 | page=}}</ref>

==Other projects==
In 2018, in a project of exploration of the archives of the Jodrell Bank Observatory, Prof. Novoselov helped Prof. Tim O'Brian to transcribe radio transmission (most possibly simulated instrument reading) from the Soviet [[Zond 6]] received by radio telescope at [[Jodrell Bank Observatory]] in November 1968.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.jodrellbank.net/50-year-old-audio-archive-of-soviet-zond-6-lunar-mission-released-by-jodrell-bank/|title=Audio archive of Soviet Zond 6 lunar mission released by Jodrell Bank|access-date=2019-12-14|language=en}}</ref><sup>,</sup><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.jb.man.ac.uk//multimedia/audio/library/zond6.pdf|title=Transcript of Jodrell Bank recordings of Russian probe Zond 6 from November 1968|access-date=2019-12-14|language=en}}</ref>

==Legacy==
[[File:Manchester Alumni.jpg|thumb|Novoselov's name in the Manchester University notable alumni pavement]]
* Novoselov International Materials Award - the award has been established in honor of the lifetime achievements of Prof. Sir, Konstantin Novoselov. The purpose of this Award is to acknowledge the extraordinary and groundbreaking scientific achievements from scientists and engineers in the field of Materials, within the FLOGEN Sustainability Framework. The Award Citation reads:
"For Leadership in developing and applying new materials methods and technologies for a sustainable development in the environmental, economic, and social points of view".<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.flogen.org/?p=177#toop|title=Novoselov International Materials Award}}</ref>
* Novoselov received a named plaque in the Bicentenary Way - notable alumni pavement at the University of Manchester.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.manchester.ac.uk/about/bicentenary/bicentenary-way/|title=Bicentenary Way}}</ref>
* In 2026 Konstantin Novoselov received a named bench at the National Central University in Taiwan.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://ncusec.ncu.edu.tw/news/en/headlines_content.php?H_ID=4759|title=Nobel Laureate Konstantin Novoselov Visits NCU, Joining the University’s Legacy of Scientific Excellence|date=September 24, 2026}}</ref>

==Art involvement==
Novoselov is known for his interest in art.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.oeaw.ac.at/oesterreichische-akademie-der-wissenschaften/die-oeaw/article/bridging-two-cultures-1/|title=Bridging Two Cultures|access-date=2018-01-18|language=de|archive-date=19 January 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180119060611/https://www.oeaw.ac.at/oesterreichische-akademie-der-wissenschaften/die-oeaw/article/bridging-two-cultures-1/|url-status=dead}}</ref> He practices in Chinese traditional drawing<ref name="china.org.cn">[http://china.org.cn/world/Off_the_Wire/2015-09/29/content_36704513.htm Joint painting exhibition of Chinese diplomat, British Nobel laureate kicks off.] Xinhua, 29 September 2015</ref> and has been involved in several projects on modern art.<ref name="BBC News">{{cite news|last1=Youngs|first1=Ian|title=Art and science collide to reopen Whitworth gallery|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/entertainment-arts-31006334|work=BBC News |access-date=2016-10-10|date=12 February 2015}}</ref> 
Thus, in February 2015 he combined forces with [[Cornelia Parker]] to create a display for the opening of the [[Whitworth Art Gallery]]. Cornelia Parker's meteorite shower firework (pieces of meteorites loaded in firework) was launched by Novoselov breathing on graphene gas sensor (which changed the resistance of graphene due to doping by water vapour). [[Graphene]] was obtained through exfoliation of [[graphite]] which was extracted from a drawing of [[William Blake]]. Novoselov suggested that he also exfoliated graphite obtained from the drawings of other prominent artists: [[John Constable]], [[Pablo Picasso]], [[J. M. W. Turner]], [[Thomas Girtin]]. He said that only microscopic amounts (flake size less than 100 micrometres) was extracted from each of the drawings.<ref name="BBC News"/> In 2015 he participated in "in conversation" session with [[Douglas Gordon]] during Interdependence session at [[Manchester International Festival]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Artist Douglas Gordon and Professor Kostya Novoselov in conversation|url=http://www.interdependence.co.com|website=interdependence.co.com|access-date=2016-10-10}}</ref>

[[File:Konstantin Novoselov Chinese painting 2015.jpg|thumb|Novoselov while painting at the residence of Chinese Consul General Li in Manchester.]]

He also participates in discussions on the relation between art and science. Novoselov believes that artists and scientists both rely on curiosity, willingness to learn and imagination:
{{centred pull quote|Artists and scientists both think outside the box. They've got to come with genius experiments or ideas to expose the most interesting phenomena. Later, they've got to diverge a little bit because scientists will start to look at the common elements between many of the phenomena to describe the most general law, and artists will probably try to study individuals rather than the crowd as a whole. But we're just two sides of the same medal.<ref name="BBC News"/>}}

Novoselov is fond of Chinese calligraphy and drawing.<ref name="china.org.cn"/> He learned it from a prominent Chinese artist [[Zheng Shenglong]]. Nine ink paintings by Prof. Novoselov were shown at the exhibition "Britain Through the Eyes of a Chinese Diplomat" at the University of Leeds.<ref>{{cite news|title=Art has no boundaries: the Grand Opening of 'Britain Through the Eyes of a Chinese Diplomat|url=http://lubswww.leeds.ac.uk/confucius/news/item/articles/2015/September/art-has-no-boundaries-the-grand-opening-of-britain-through-the-eyes-of-a-chinese-diplomat/|publisher=The Business Confucius Institute at the University of Leeds|date=30 September 2015|access-date=10 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161011054638/http://lubswww.leeds.ac.uk/confucius/news/item/articles/2015/September/art-has-no-boundaries-the-grand-opening-of-britain-through-the-eyes-of-a-chinese-diplomat/|archive-date=11 October 2016|url-status=dead}}</ref>
One of his paintings is now in the collection of [[Xi Jinping]], the [[General Secretary of the Chinese Communist Party]] since 2012.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Durani|first1=Matin|title=Immersive art, physics pumpkins, personalizing Thor's hammer and more|url=http://blog.physicsworld.com/2015/10/23/immersive-art-physics-pumpkins-personalising-thors-hammer-and-more/#more-13133|publisher=physicsworld.com|access-date=2016-10-10|date=23 October 2015}}</ref>

Novoselov participated in [[Viennacontemporary]] in 2017,<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=http://www.viennacontemporary.at/en/program/online-catalogue/|title=Catalogue {{!}} viennacontemporary|website=www.viennacontemporary.at|language=en-US|access-date=2018-05-20|archive-date=20 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180520194237/http://www.viennacontemporary.at/en/program/online-catalogue/|url-status=dead}}</ref> where 5 of his works have been presented by RDI.Creative gallery. The paintings presented a range of topics, from the very traditional Chinese paintings to landscapes to contemporary subjects. It is claimed that graphene ink has been used in at least some of those paintings.<ref name="auto"/>

In 2025, Novoselov curated an exhibition at [[Venice Biennale]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.labiennale.org/en/architecture/2025/natural/material-bank-matters-make-sense/ |title=Material Bank: Matters Make Sense |date=2 June 2025 |access-date=2 June 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Novoselov holds both Russian and British citizenship.<ref>{{citation | title = Graphene pioneers bag Nobel prize | url = http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/news/43939 | newspaper = Physics World | date = 5 October 2010 | access-date = 5 October 2010 | archive-date = 8 October 2010 | archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20101008071254/http://physicsworld.com/cws/article/news/43939 | url-status = dead }}</ref> He is married and has two daughters.<ref name="whoswho"/> He is an agnostic.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.themoscowtimes.com/q-n-a/article/qa-russian-nobel-laureate-on-fun-god-and-the-ideal-physicist/508735.html|title=Q&A: Russian Nobel Laureate on Fun, God and the 'Ideal Physicist'|date=9 October 2014 |access-date=31 October 2017}}</ref>

== Political positions ==
In February 2022, he signed an open letter by Russian scientists condemning the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://t-invariant.org/2022/02/we-are-against-war/ |title=Открытое письмо российских учёных и научных журналистов против войны с Украиной |date=24 February 2022 |access-date=2 April 2022 |language=ru |trans-title=An open letter from Russian scientists and scientific journalist against the war in Ukraine}}</ref>
